class.name: TransitionScreen
class.brief_description: Root of a scene that covers the screen while the next scene loads, then changes to it.
class.description: A transition screen is the root node of a scene you design like any other (a [ColorRect] background, a logo, a [ProgressBar]). Added to the [SceneTree], it runs one transition and frees itself: 1. On its first frame it emits [signal started] and starts loading [member next_scene] in the background with [method ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request] (and [member preload_assets] with [method ResourceDatabase.preload_from]). 2. It fades in over the current scene for [member fade_in_duration] seconds. 3. While fully visible it emits [signal progress_changed] and, when everything is loaded, [signal loaded] (or [signal load_failed], then it fades out without changing the scene). It waits at least [member min_duration] seconds (or until [method finish] is called, or a key, mouse button, touch or joypad button is pressed if [member skippable] is [code]true[/code]). 4. It changes the scene with [method SceneTree.change_scene_to_packed] while it is fully visible, so the old scene is never seen again. 5. It fades out over the new scene for [member fade_out_duration] seconds, emits [signal finished] and frees itself. The easiest way to start a transition is [method SceneTree.change_scene_with_transition]. A transition screen can also be the current scene (opened with [method SceneTree.change_scene_to_file], or the boot splash): it detaches itself from [member SceneTree.current_scene] before the change and stays for the fade-out. A screen added inside the current scene moves itself to the tree root before it starts, so it is not removed with the old scene. With an empty [member next_scene] it only fades in, waits and fades out, as an overlay. Only one transition runs at a time: [method SceneTree.change_scene_with_transition] returns [constant ERR_BUSY] while one runs, and a second screen added to the tree prints an error and frees itself without doing anything. From the start of the fade-in until the scene has changed, the screen marks every input event as handled in [method Node._input], so the covered scene (and the screen's own [Control]s) receive no input; skip inputs still work. The fade modulates the whole layer (all children together, their own [member CanvasItem.modulate] stays untouched). Override [method _update_fade] for code-driven animations, or set [member animation_player], [member intro_animation] and [member outro_animation] to play an [AnimationPlayer] animation instead of the fade (each of the two phases separately; the built-in fade stays the default). In the editor the screen is shown fully visible and does nothing. It runs while the tree is paused ([member Node.process_mode] is [constant Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS]). Durations are in scaled time: with an [member Engine.time_scale] of [code]0.0[/code] the transition does not advance. See [LoadingScreen] for a progress bar and tips, and [SplashScreen] for the boot splash. [b]Note:[/b] Without threads (the default Web export) [method ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request] loads on the main thread. The screen therefore starts loading only on the frame after it became fully visible, and the whole load is one blocking step: the game shows the screen's last frame (animations, tips and the progress bar stop) until the scene is loaded, and [method get_progress] jumps from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. For a boot splash this means the splash is drawn first, then the main scene loads, then [member min_duration] runs. [b]Note:[/b] A [CanvasModulate] inside the screen replaces the fade, as both set the modulate of the layer's canvas.

method.name: _update_fade
create_template
method.description: Returns a ready-made screen scene to start from, or [code]null[/code] if it cannot be built. All nodes are owned by the root, so it saves as a normal scene. It reads the project settings [code]application/boot_splash/bg_color[/code], [code]application/boot_splash/image[/code], [code]application/config/icon[/code] and [code]application/config/name[/code]; the text color follows the brightness of the background. The scene has a [ColorRect] [code]Background[/code] in the color of [code]application/boot_splash/bg_color[/code], the project logo ([code]application/boot_splash/image[/code], else [code]application/config/icon[/code], else the project name as a [Label]), and an [AnimationPlayer] with the animations [code]intro[/code] and [code]outro[/code] set as [member intro_animation] and [member outro_animation] (the background and the content fade). [constant TEMPLATE_SPLASH] has a [SplashScreen] root. [constant TEMPLATE_LOADING] has a [LoadingScreen] root with a tip label, a [ProgressBar] and a count label, all set up. In the editor, [b]Project > Tools > Create Splash Screen Scene...[/b] and [b]Create Loading Screen Scene...[/b] save these scenes to a file you choose and open them; a splash scene can be set as [member ProjectSettings.application/boot_splash/scene] right away. [codeblocks] [gdscript] var scene = TransitionScreen.create_template(TransitionScreen.TEMPLATE_LOADING) ResourceSaver.save(scene, "res://loading_screen.tscn") [/gdscript] [csharp] var scene = TransitionScreen.CreateTemplate(TransitionScreen.Template.Loading); ResourceSaver.Save(scene, "res://loading_screen.tscn"); [/csharp] [/codeblocks]

method.name: finish
method.description: Changes the scene as soon as everything is loaded, without waiting for the rest of [member min_duration]. Needed when [member auto_finish] is [code]false[/code], for example for a "Press any key" prompt after [signal loaded].

method.name: get_fade
method.description: Returns the current visibility of the screen, from [code]0.0[/code] (transparent) to [code]1.0[/code] (fully visible).

method.name: get_load_error
method.description: Returns [constant OK], or the error of the last failed load or scene change (see [signal load_failed]).

method.name: get_load_progress
method.description: Returns the files loaded and the total as a [LoadProgress], the same model as [signal ResourceDatabase.preload_progress]: [member next_scene] counts as one file next to the files of [member preload_assets] (its [member Preloads.paths] and the files of its [member Preloads.manifests]). The ratio is [method get_progress].

method.name: get_progress
method.description: Returns the load progress from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]: the progress of all files together, each file weighing the same ([member next_scene] is one file next to the files of [member preload_assets]), so it agrees with the counts of [method get_load_progress]. It is [code]1.0[/code] only when everything is loaded.

method.name: get_state
method.description: Returns the current step of the transition.

members.member: Path to the [AnimationPlayer] that plays [member intro_animation] and [member outro_animation], relative to the screen (usually a child of it). An animation that cannot report its end runs as the built-in fade instead (a warning is printed): an animation without length, a looping one, a player with speed [code]0[/code], a player that does not process (paused or disabled) or one in manual callback mode. A phase ends when the player emits [signal AnimationMixer.animation_finished]; if that never comes, it ends one second after the animation length.

If [code]true[/code], the scene changes as soon as everything is loaded and [member min_duration] has passed. If [code]false[/code], the screen waits for [method finish] (or a skip input if [member skippable] is [code]true[/code]).
Seconds the screen takes to fade in over the current scene. [code]0.0[/code] shows it at once.
Seconds the screen takes to fade out over the new scene. [code]0.0[/code] hides it at once.

If [code]true[/code], the current scene is freed as soon as the screen is fully visible, and [member next_scene] starts loading on the next frame. The old and the new scene are never in memory together, which helps on mobile and Web; loading starts a little later. If loading then fails, no scene is left in the tree.

Name of the animation of [member animation_player] that replaces the built-in fade-in. The fade-in is over when the animation has played ([member fade_in_duration] is ignored; the length is divided by the player's [member AnimationPlayer.speed_scale]). The animation must cover the screen, because the covered scene changes right after it. While it plays the layer is opaque and [method _update_fade] is not called; [method get_fade] runs from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code] with the animation. If empty, or the animation or the player is not found (a warning is printed), the built-in fade runs.
Minimum seconds the screen stays fully visible before the scene changes, even if loading is done earlier.

Path or UID of the scene ([code].tscn[/code], [code].scn[/code] or [code].res[/code]) to change to. If empty, no scene change happens: the screen fades in, waits [member min_duration] and fades out. [SplashScreen] uses [member ProjectSettings.application/run/main_scene] instead. A screen never loads its own scene file.

Name of the animation of [member animation_player] that replaces the built-in fade-out, played after the scene has changed. It must uncover the new scene (slide away, dissolve). The screen is freed when the animation has played ([member fade_out_duration] is ignored); [method get_fade] runs from [code]1.0[/code] to [code]0.0[/code] with it. If empty, or not found, the built-in fade runs (starting opaque, also after an animated intro).

Optional assets that are loaded into the [ResourceDatabase] with [method ResourceDatabase.preload_from] while the screen loads [member next_scene]. The scene changes only after [signal ResourceDatabase.preload_finished] for these [Preloads]. Their progress ([signal ResourceDatabase.preload_progress]) counts into [method get_progress] with the same weight as the scene. Without thread support the files load one per frame while the screen is drawn.
If [code]true[/code], a pressed key, mouse button (not the wheel), touch or joypad button emits [signal skipped] and calls [method finish]. The scene still changes only when everything is loaded.

signal.name: finished
signal.description: Emitted when the screen has faded out (over the new scene, or over the unchanged scene after [signal load_failed]), right before it frees itself.

signal.name: load_failed
signal.description: Emitted instead of [signal loaded] when [member next_scene] cannot be loaded, or after [signal loaded] when the loaded scene cannot be instantiated. The scene does not change and the screen fades out over the current scene. With [member free_current_scene_before_loading] the old scene is already freed, so no scene is left: connect to this signal to change to a fallback scene. See [method get_load_error].

signal.name: loaded
signal.description: Emitted once when [member next_scene] and [member preload_assets] are loaded. Not emitted when loading fails (see [signal load_failed]).

signal.name: progress_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the load progress changes, with a value from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. See [method get_progress].

signal.name: skipped
signal.description: Emitted when a skip input was pressed while [member skippable] is [code]true[/code].

signal.name: started
signal.description: Emitted on the first frame of the screen in the tree, when loading starts and the fade-in begins.

constants.constant: Not started yet (or in the editor).
Fading in over the current scene.
Fully visible, everything loaded; waiting for [member min_duration] or [method finish].
The scene has changed (or loading failed); fading out.
Done; the screen is freed at the end of the frame.
A splash screen: [SplashScreen] root with the project logo.
A loading screen: [LoadingScreen] root with the logo, tips, a progress bar and a count label.
Represents the size of the [enum Template] enum.
